Formulation:  
Mary Smith, a 28-year-old female without previous medical or psychiatric history, presents with an acute onset unilateral (left posterior) throbbing headache rated 8/10 in severity. Family history positive for maternal migraines and hypertension. No systemic or neurological symptoms indicative of acute infection or intracranial event. No recent stressors or lifestyle changes reported. Clinical presentation and DDx favor migraine headache as the primary diagnosis, despite absence of aura. Psychological distress is minimal but patient reports subjective difficulty concentrating and working due to pain. Protective psychosocial factors include stable living situation with partner and absence of substance use. The headache is precipitating functional impairment in work and daily activities. Close monitoring and symptomatic treatment recommended.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: New onset severe unilateral headache (probable migraine) causing functional impairment  
- Patient Goal(s):  
  - Achieve effective headache relief  
  - Return to normal work and daily functioning  
- Clinical Goal(s):  
  - Provide adequate pain control  
  - Monitor for development of new neurological or systemic symptoms  
  - Prevent worsening functional impairment  
- Actions (Patient):  
  - Take prescribed medication (stronger analgesic and paracetamol) regularly with food  
  - Maintain hydration and rest  
  - Report any worsening symptoms or new symptoms such as fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):  
  - Prescribe stronger analgesic (specific medication not documented) and paracetamol with dosage instructions  
  - Provide advice on hydration, rest, and warning signs requiring urgent review  
  - Advise follow-up call if symptoms persist beyond 1–2 days or worsen  

Secondary Problem: Not applicable  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:  
- Education Given: Yes  
- Topics Covered: Headache management, medication use (ibuprofen avoidance concurrent), hydration, rest, signs of serious illness (fever, neck stiffness, rash), and when to seek urgent medical attention  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: New or worsening headache severity, fever, vomiting, rash, neck stiffness, new neurological symptoms  
- Coping Strategies: Rest and hydration

- Migraine headache — Likelihood: High  
  Justification: Unilateral throbbing headache, severe intensity (8/10), family history of migraines, absence of systemic or neurological symptoms, no relief with ibuprofen
